utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, have the accused brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can now resume our work. I would like to say good morning to the interpreters and make sure everybody is at his or her station, as usual. Good morning. Everyone is here. The Defence is here, the Prosecution, the accused is here. The Judges are also here, and that's important, and so we can begin. Mr. Greaves, I give the floor to you for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. I call Witness DA, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you hear me, Witness DA? We're going to call you "DA". Do you hear me? Please turn to the Presiding Judge. I'm speaking to you. Do you hear me? Do you see me? Good morning. I'm the Presiding Judge. For the time being, I'm the Presiding Judge. All right. Please try to relax. First you're going to be sure that your name is the one that's on this document that is being given to you. Don't state it. Simply check to see that it is, in fact, your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Remain standing to take an oath. You're going to read the oath which is being given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may now be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please sit down. Make yourself comfortable. Try and relax. You're in front of Judges. You have nothing to fear. You are being protected by measures which are taken at the request of the Defence for you, and you're going to answer Mr. Greaves' question, who is Defence counsel for Goran Jelisic, who is in this courtroom on your left. Then you will answer the Prosecutor's questions, and finally those of the Judges. Mr. Greaves, please proceed. Examined by Mr. Greaves:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DA, could you tell us, please, what your ethnic background is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I am Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first meet Goran --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think it's possible that the witness's microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The microphone is connected.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry, I just wanted to make certain all was in order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first meet Goran Jelisic, please, Witness DA?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise, but the microphone is not working properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you sure that the microphone is working properly? I've got the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Insofar as the voice is being distorted, it isn't the microphone that is usually used but the microphone which is a little bit larger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, all right. Can the interpreters hear? Do they hear the answers, do they hear the witness's answers? All right. Everything seems to be in its proper place, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it that you first met Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I first met Goran at a fishing competition, because my job is linked to that particular sport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And having met him whilst out fishing, did you meet him again on similar occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Later on, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Goran Jelisic part of a fishing team for the purposes of these competitions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic make-up of his team? Was it mixed or one race only; can you help us about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: The team was mixed, just as the town of Bijeljina is mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, as a result of meeting him through these fishing competitions, become friendly with Goran?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I became friends with him because Goran grew up in the town where my brother-in-law grew up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now to the time when the former Yugoslavia began to break up. Did your friendship with him continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time during the course of your friendship with him, did he ever express to you any nationalist or extremist sentiments towards other races?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: He never said anything bad about any of the nationalities. Otherwise, he would not be friends with me and my family, because I belong to a different ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever show any interest in politics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I never noticed that in Goran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as his personal disposition was concerned, was he a happy individual, or sad, or introverted, extraverted? How would you describe him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: As a young man, Goran was very communicative, a happy man. He liked socialising. That's how I know him, and that's why I was very surprised with all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As matters began to deteriorate in the former Yugoslavia, did he ever express any views about what was apparently taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: No. He believed that the politicians would settle it all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you knew him before the war, did he have any girlfriends that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Goran had a lot of friends among the Muslims, and he had a girlfriend, too, who was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war broke out, did you have to do any military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Yes. We were all drafted by the military authorities, and as a citizen, I too was mobilised and was sent to the Majevica front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between March and December of 1992, did you see Goran at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I did not see Goran during that period of time. Sometime before the new year of 1993, I met him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you resume your old friendship with him at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you visit each other's homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Goran would frequently come by with my brother-in-law. I live in the country, in a village, and they are friends from their school days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had his attitude towards you and your family changed in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I didn't notice any changes at all, and I had the impression that he was even better in his behaviour towards me, and he asked me whether anybody had insulted me because I was of a different ethnic group, nationality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever offer you any help or assistance of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Yes, he said that if there was anything he could do to help me, he said he would as far as he was able to. I was grateful to him for that, as well as my family, because after all, it was wartime, and I come from a different nationality and lived in that town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those offers of assistance, did that impress you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, like anybody else, you always feel gratified if somebody offers to help you, although I probably didn't expect any help from him because he was not able to do very much, just like any other ordinary person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your conversations with him, did he express any attitude about the war and what had happened during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, he would say that it was all mindless and futile and that it should be finished as soon as possible; that it was the politicians that started it and that they would profit, whereas the people to suffer were the ordinary people, whereas the rest would -- the politicians would continue to profit from it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would he remain calm during such conversations, or did the topic upset him in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I noticed that after that kind of conversation, he would become upset and raise his voice slightly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that there had been an element of persecution towards the Muslims in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Goran ever make any observations about that persecution, that policy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I never heard that personally from Goran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to turn now to the winter of 1994. Is one of the things that you do at home is to cure meat, Witness DA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: That particular winter, the winter of 1994, because I had heard the rumours going around which were spreading -- and Bijeljina is a small town, so you can hear everything and hear it quickly -- I learned that allegedly Goran had killed some people. And when we finished our job and when everybody went into the house, the two of us stayed outside alone. While we were putting away the tools, I felt uncomfortable, because I wanted to know if it was true. So I asked Goran. I said, "Goran, is it really true?" And he was a little surprised, when I asked him that, and said, "Uncle [redacted], it is the bitter truth that I really did kill ten people, following orders by certain individuals." And he said, "Because of that I am very sorry, because I don't think those people were guilty of anything." And he said that he hoped that one day everybody would take responsibility for what they had done and for the people who forced me [sic] to do that, too. We ended our conversation there. I was terribly surprised, and I felt very sorry for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he identify anybody who had been responsible for giving him such orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, he told me that the chief of SUP in Brcko, where that happened, a certain Dragan -- whether the surname was Veselic, I don't quite remember, and another name that I don't recall because after all, a lot of time has passed since then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything of what had happened to him since that time, since the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: He did tell me and I heard that he was persecuted, the police, a Davidovic, and he didn't want to go any more. And he even injured himself. He wounded himself in the leg, and he showed me some of his wounds. And I knew that he didn't want to continue to do what he was being forced to do. And as far as I know, for a time he fled to Serbia, as well, to prevent them from capturing him and liquidating him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of what he was telling you, did he remain calm, or did his demeanour change? Was he upset in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, of course he was upset. Anybody would be upset after a conversation of that kind or when you're forced to do things of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you about the effect which the events of the war had had upon him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, he said he had no intention of harming anybody, but it transpired that you can lose your head very easily during a war, and that he was forced and pressured into doing what he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any conversation about any repercussions upon him since these events had happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, quite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll move on. Were you surprised by what you had heard from him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Of course I was surprised. I didn't expect it from such a nice young man, that it was possible that he could have done anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, had he ever exhibited any sign whatever that he was someone capable of doing these things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: As far as I knew him, no. He did not show any such signs. And he was friends with my brother-in-law, as I say, where they grew up, in Bijeljina, which is a small town. Of course rumours go around very quickly, and I never heard of anything like that, and his demeanour was not that of a young man like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The killings of which you heard from him, and no doubt you've heard other rumours, were those things that you condemn, Witness DA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, every right-minded person would condemn every killing, and everybody must be held accountable for what he has done. This cannot be avoided, either in the eyes of men and in the eyes of God, or before the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your conclusion about the character of Goran Jelisic in the light of what he admitted to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, all I can say in conclusion is that he was forced to do this as a young person, and how -- but how he was forced to do this, I don't know. But I do believe that that young man would not have done it had he not been forced to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes, Witness DA. Would you wait there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Greaves. Let me turn to the Office of the Prosecutor. The Prosecutor is now going to ask you some questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other possibility, Witness DA, is that you were misled by Jelisic and he was entirely willing to kill these people. That's a possibility, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I don't know that. I can't say that. I can't make that kind of conclusion about anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to know why you say that you felt sorry for him, but so far you've said nothing about feeling sorry for the victims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I said that I was sorry for every man, every young man and every victim. It was war. I am very sorry for everybody who suffered during the war, and particularly as many young people died during the war for nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you be forced to kill another man, please, Witness DA? Explain that to us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, I think you can be bribed. I didn't have any problems. I was an old man, I worked in a warehouse, but I heard rumours going around town that this kind of thing was happening on all three sides, not only on our side and not only in Goran's case but in others too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: People would simply be paid, be bribed to kill; is that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Blackmailed. The witness said "blackmailed".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, blackmailed. Well, are you suggesting that Jelisic was blackmailed, and if so, over what topic was he being blackmailed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I know that he was forced. How he was forced, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know the man was forced if he never told you, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, he did tell me. He said he was forced. He was made to by the person that ordered him, Dragan, the chief of that SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you say to him, "How on Earth did he persuade you, how on Earth did he force you?" You must have been so shocked, you must have asked that question, Witness DA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: That's right, I was shocked, and I was completely taken aback and was speechless. I can't explain it. I didn't know what to ask him. I just shut up, and that's where we concluded that very uncomfortable, unfortunate conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many seconds was it that you discussed this topic with Jelisic on the basis of which you come here to give evidence of his good character? Was it 10 seconds, 15 seconds, one minute? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: The conversation with Goran himself, that particular conversation? Well, I know Goran, and that's why I was so surprised to hear what he told me. I didn't discuss his character with him but what he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the conversation, where he said he was forced to kill, how long did that conversation last, Witness DA; half a minute, a minute?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, not half a minute. Two or three minutes, perhaps, while we came to the topic from my last question to his answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the basis of all that he said in two or three minutes, you feel able to come here and say he must have been forced and he's a man of good character; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: With respect, that's an unfair question. This man has known him for ten or more years. Surely, the proper question would be to ask him, "In the context of knowing him for that period of time, how are you able to assess this element of character?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will make that decision. I think that's a relevant question. Please continue, Mr. Nice. The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How, on the basis of two or three minutes of conversation, are you able to come here and say this man was forced and that your judgement of his character remains as you have described it, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am not making any judgement or decision or assessing anybody's character. But having known him from a long time back, I came here to say what happened. I know that people are saying that many young men like that were forced to do similar things on all three sides, not only on this one, whether it was on the Serbian side, the Muslim side, or any other side, and many young men lost their lives and committed things like that during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forced to do what, Witness DA? What is it that this man, as you understood it, did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did he kill people simply by being a soldier; did he kill people by taking them out and executing them when he had been given proper formal instructions to execute them; did he take them out at random from a warehouse, line them up against a wall, select one, make him put his head on a drain, and blow his brains out? What is it this man, as you understood it, was forced to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: He was forced, as a soldier, to execute military orders, which if you do not execute them, you lose your head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you he was executing military orders or did you guess that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, I guessed it because I know that that's how it was, because nobody will kill anybody else unless he is forced to or ordered to do so from certain parties or by someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, what, these killings, as you understood it, were they in the field of war or were they somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: As far as I know, it happened in the war areas where the fighting was going on. I don't know about any other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look, please, at Exhibit 67? It's the sequence of photographs. It's already been produced as an exhibit. We're familiar with this exhibit, Witness DA. Just look at the first photograph and then cast your eyes through --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: They can stay in the book. It's all right. He can go straight through them. THE USHER: Do you want them on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, why not. Put them on the ELMO. And the next photograph. The man in the blue shirt is Jelisic. The next photograph, please. The next photograph, please. The next photograph, please. The next photograph, please. Pause there for one minute, but we'll look at the next photographs in a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Jelisic killing a man in the street. You had no idea, when you gave evidence of his character, that this is the sort of thing he had done, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: First of all, judging by this photograph, I cannot say whether it's Jelisic or not, because it's taken from behind and it could be anyone. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's admitted that it's him. He's admitted it. It's a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness, I want to confirm what the Prosecutor said. The identification -- well, all right. The fact that you can't identify it is right, but I want to tell you that the Judges in this Trial Chamber received testimony corroborating the fact that this is Goran Jelisic. I want this to be clear to you. Of course, it is your own right to say that you don't recognise him. Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no idea, did you, that Jelisic killed people in the circumstances revealed in this photograph, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Jelisic has also said that he was incapable of looking at the people he killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Would you turn over the next photograph, please, usher?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see him there? Please look at the photograph, Witness, and the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're going to have to bend it over there. Yes, that's better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next photograph, please. Do you see what he's doing? He's aiming at the head of the man that's on the ground. And the next photograph, please. Aiming and looking at the man dead or dying. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I see the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no idea, did you, that the man about whom you've come to give character evidence was capable of doing this sort of thing, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am talking about what happened before. What happened there, I don't know what happened. I know nothing of that, and I cannot bring any conclusions in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. The exhibit can be removed. Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He spoke to you in critical terms of the profit made in war by the leaders, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Yes. He said that all the leaders were profiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he imply by that that he had himself made no profit from war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: That's what I concluded, judging by the conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he made no admission to you about the money that he had taken from Muslim victims of the attack on Muslims by Serbs, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I didn't ask him about that; neither did he tell me anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He made no revelation to you of where he got the money from on which he was living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say he expressed no views adverse to Muslims, although he did ask you whether you had been insulted, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, he didn't only ask me. I know that he helped many of the Muslims whom he had been friends with. He helped them during the war and during the fighting. I did not hear him take money from anyone. What happened at the front, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, he's made it clear, in answers he's given on a tape-recorder to investigators, that it was explained to him that the people he had to kill were Muslim agitators and extremists and that that's how he was persuaded to kill Muslims, people called balijas. He never gave that explanation to you, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "Yes", you're, I think, agreeing with my proposition that he didn't ever give you that explanation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: He never told me why he killed, except for the fact that I learned that he was forced. And the rest, I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you learned, you learned from his lips and from nowhere else that he was forced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I can give you the following answer to this question: I concluded that he was pressured into doing this because I know that other people were pressured to do things that were improper, illegal, and those people ended up at the Tribunal, people from all three sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which people, then, just so that we understand your position? Which people have landed up at the Tribunal who shouldn't be here, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I didn't say "people who shouldn't be here". It is not for me to say who should be here or who shouldn't be. I just know that some people are guilty of higher crimes than other people. I am just saying -- I'm just stating that some people were forced to do certain things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us about his having a girlfriend. Just one small detail. Was he proud of his success with women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Sir, I'm an elderly person. I just heard rumours. I know that he had friends among Muslims and that he had a girlfriend who was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he proud of his prowess with women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I have not observed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... been seen by other people preparatory to coming to judgement, and his attitude on women, part of his character, is summarised by his saying he took test drives on many women. Is that something he ever said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He spoke of killing a precise number of people. Please tell us how many.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: He told me ten, twelve people, although he did say, "I don't know if they were guilty or not. I feel sorry for those people. I don't know which ones were guilty and which ones were not, but I did it based on the orders of Dragan, the commander in MUP."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's ten or twelve people. Could it be more than twelve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I could not have concluded that. Ten, twelve people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what he made quite clear to you was that the people he killed might have been completely innocent, for he knew nothing to show that they were guilty of anything; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. He made it clear to you that the people he killed might have been completely innocent, for he knew nothing to show that they were guilty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: He said he didn't know whether those people were guilty or not. He simply carried on his orders. That's all he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Greaves, you have the right to reexamine in order to supplement any of the questions that the Prosecutor asked. All right. Mr. Greaves is going to take the floor again, Witness DA, before the Judges ask their questions. Re-examined by Mr. Greaves:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DA, you have been shown some photographs this morning. Do those photographs in any way alter the element of surprise that you have that Goran Jelisic could be involved in those sort of events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Looking at these photographs, I cannot conclude that Goran is in these pictures. This is not -- these photographs are not very clear. I don't know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DA, just remember, it's accepted that the person in that photograph is Goran Jelisic. Just listen to the question: Do those photographs alter your surprise that Goran Jelisic could be involved in events of that kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: They do not alter, because I know that he did it because he was ordered to. And, of course, I feel sorry for people that were killed in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness DA. I've been listening very carefully to your defence of Mr. Jelisic. I would like you to remember that you are here as a witness, not as a defence lawyer, and you're not coming here to speak to us about human nature. Most of your answers were concerning human nature, because you are a good man, apparently, so you always would say, for instance, when you were asked if Jelisic was upset, you said, "Of course. Everybody would be upset." We are not asking about everybody. You said, when you were asked "What do you think about his killing," you said, "Of course he must have been pressured because nobody else would do it otherwise." These are quotes. "Nobody can do this unless he is pressured." So most of your answers concerned human nature. And you are coming here just to testify on very specific facts of an accused man, so we want to know three things. How long did you know Mr. Jelisic, to testify about his character? Apart from the fact that you like him, which is very clear; you even refuse to accept that the pictures are his when he has himself accepted it, and it's very commendable of you when you trust him so much. But we want to know, how long did you know him, to trust him so much? How much do you know about the events which happened? Because you seemed to look at the pictures for the first time. And you are a witness, and "witness" means somebody who saw. And really, what did you hear from him? Not from human nature. Don't tell us, "Of course everybody would be" -- whatever you said -- "everybody would be upset." No, we want to know, did you see him repenting, crying, as some people do, asking for forgiveness from the Church, from anybody? We want these facts. You are a witness of facts, not a moralist. So if you have just a few things to add, to tell us exactly how much you have known him, how much he told you, how much you have seen from these things, pictures which you don't know about, and how much you have heard from him, could you tell us something about that? Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: As I have said, I have known Goran since 1980 [sic]. We met in competitions through hunting, through fishing. And I also want to say that he became upset after I asked him the question. He blushed, he was taken aback, and he said, "I know that I will be held accountable sooner or later before the Court for this, but then I will not hide anything, and I will say about everybody who participated in it." And this is where we ended our conversation about this topic. So I felt uncomfortable, and I was surprised, and -- I don't know how to describe this, but that is just the kind of person I am. I simply could not take any more discussion of this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said, if I understood rightly, you knew him since 1980? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And since then, if you know him well, do you know what he has been doing in life? Do you know about that, or you were just going together fishing, outside? Do you know more about his life, his actions? Do you know something about that? To know his character, you should know what he has been doing. So can you tell us about that, in brief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I personally don't know what he did in life. He was a young man, and I was in such a position that I only would meet him during these fishing expeditions, competitions, and I would see him fishing, by the water. I don't know about his private life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So he was a fishing partner? That's what you know about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I am in charge of fishing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. Then he was fishing in your domain. Now let's speak about the events which happened. How close were you to all these events, or did you just hear about it from him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: I heard about -- I only heard about that. I did not stay in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. Then the last thing, how much did he talk to you about it, so that you would know exactly how he felt? Did he confide in you, as an uncle or somebody, or was it just a casual conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: When I asked the question, of course it was a casual conversation. I wanted to know whether it was true or not, because I was surprised that a young man like that could have done something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Apparently you are a very good man. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Riad. Judge Rodrigues has no questions; I have only one. You have come to testify for Goran Jelisic, and I have to congratulate you on the effort that you have made in order to testify for a criminal who has acknowledged what he has done, as he pleaded guilty to a certain number of crimes, and as Judge Riad said, we have to salute you for that, because it's never easy, but you must have said, "I have to come to speak for that man, who is in great difficulties." That's fine, but what raises questions in my mind gives me the liberty to ask you one question only: When you leave this Tribunal, will you be the same man in respect of Goran Jelisic that you were when you came into this courtroom? Will you be the same man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: If I ever meet him, if I were to meet him ever again, I don't know how that would affect my attitude to him. He will be held accountable for what he had done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Therefore you are a man of a great moral rectitude, moral principles, but these moral principles come in after friendship and fishing expeditions; is that what you are telling us? You have the right to say that. Is that what you mean, that the friendship with somebody that you would go fishing with in 1988 is the supreme barrier, which means that everything that you are shown in no way changes the idea that you have of Goran Jelisic? In other words, tomorrow, say that he would be acquitted; let's say that he would be freed, so you would be able to go fishing with him without any problems. You would be serene, you would be comfortable. Is that what you are telling us? Please answer: Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, I'm not fishing myself; I'm in charge of the fishing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, please, please, please, please, spare me. In such serious proceedings, please spare me such a ridiculous answer. I am asking you whether the fact that you would go fishing with him in 1988 represents a supreme barrier which allows you to completely ignore what Mr. Jelisic has acknowledged and what you saw today illustrated in front of you. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: No one can simply be so casual about it, and nobody could remain calm when hearing about this. But if -- it is my job to have a professional attitude towards all fishermen, because he will be held accountable by the Tribunal. He will be punished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are a man, really, who has compartments within your mind. I can congratulate you. You are well organised within your own mind. There are moral principles; there are fishing companions, which apparently is very important. I think I won't ask you any further questions. I simply would like to say to you, do you continue to say, those poor victims, murdered, as you saw on the photograph, when you saw them transported in refrigerated trucks like animals, Witness DA, can you continue to tell us that you are very sorry, just very sorry? Is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DA
utterances.text: Naturally, I am sorry. I could only see this in a movie. I still, to this day, cannot still believe that this had, in fact, happened. This is unbelievable. I cannot comprehend that something like this could have happened, and I'm still -- to me, this still seems impossible, although he admitted, but I'm just such a person that I simply find it difficult to believe all this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have no further questions. I send you back to your work, and I congratulate you. I believe that you are a good fisherman. All right. The testimony is complete. We will now take a break -- yes, I was just going to say -- all right. We are going to take a five- to ten-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can resume the hearing now. Have the accused brought in, please. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please stand. Do you hear me, Witness DI? First we're going to ask you to check the names that are on the piece of paper being shown you. Don't state the name. We don't want your name to be disclosed. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Please remain standing for a few more moments, as long as it takes to take an oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may now be seated, Witness DI. You have agreed to come to testify at the trial of Goran Jelisic here at the International Criminal Tribunal, Goran Jelisic who is to your left. I'm sure they explained to you. First the Defence attorney, Mr. Greaves, will ask you some questions, then the Prosecutor, and lastly the Judges. Please relax. You have nothing to fear. Remain calm, and then answer the questions that you're asked very precisely. Please proceed, Mr. Greaves. Examined by Mr. Greaves:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DI, would you be so kind as to tell us your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I'm of the Muslim nationality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first meet Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I've known Goran since I was ten years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you began to work together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I went to school with Goran together, and we worked together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start to work with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: In 198 -- I'm not quite sure which year. In 1986 or 1987, sometime there. We did agricultural work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the place where you were employed, and don't tell us what the name of it was, but at that place were the majority of workers of one particular nationality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes. They were mostly Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Goran know that you were a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness sit closer to the microphone, please, the interpreters note.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say what Goran Jelisic's attitude towards those of other nationalities was at the place where you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, there was no difference between us. We didn't distinguish between Muslims and Serbs. We were all just like one family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left the place where you were working?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, did you see somewhat less of Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war broke out, did you remain where you were living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Not exactly in that place; a little further off from it, a few kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now, please, to the summer of 1993. Did you re-establish contact with Goran Jelisic at around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes. In the summer of 1993, I saw Goran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By this time, had you become married and had at least one child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Goran Jelisic in the summer of 1993, was his attitude towards you any different from what it had been before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't change at all. In fact, he was a little better, because we hadn't seen each other for quite some time, for several months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he make any enquires about your new and present circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes, several times. He asked me how I was, whether everything was okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he enquire about how you were managing to support yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes, he asked that too as to my material status. He asked a lot of questions about my well-being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion, did you have one of your children with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did he react towards your child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, he almost considered it to be a close relation of his.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Goran Jelisic know your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he make any enquires about their circumstances and how they were getting on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes, he made enquires.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, did he begin to come to your house at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give you any financial assistance of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were things during that period for you and your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, they were highly critical. My brother was in Bosnia, and we didn't have much to live on. So with Goran and his help, we succeeded in surviving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in employment at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your husband in employment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it easy for Muslims to get jobs in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If Your Honours would give me a moment, please. Your Honour, there's an issue of interpretation. My interpreter says that the question was interpreted wrongly and that the question, as interpreted, was, "Was it difficult for Muslims to get jobs in that area at that time?" I would like to have it clarified, please, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I had understood -- well, the question was, "Was it easy for Muslims to find jobs," and the answer that was given was, "Yes." The answer is the problem; isn't that correct? All right. Ask the question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The question was wrongly interpreted, according to my interpreter. May I have Your Honour's leave to ask the question again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Or to correct it, because we'll have two contradictory questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You can correct it, if you want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DI, you've told Their Honours that neither you nor your husband were in employment at that time. As far as Muslims were concerned, was it easy or was it difficult for Muslims to get jobs at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: It was difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive financial assistance from Goran Jelisic, or other material assistance from him, during those times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I got material and financial assistance from Goran, and he was always there to help me whenever I needed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of him having helped any other Muslims at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without mentioning any names of those to whom he had given help, how many people were you aware of to whom he'd given help?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, there are several, but I'm certain for about two men, because I was present when he helped them, and they said how Goran had helped them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as his attitude towards Muslims was concerned, had that changed in any way in the later years when you knew him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Goran Jelisic has pleaded guilty before this Tribunal to committing a substantial number of killings and other offences. Before you came here today, were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, just a little. But you know what, Goran, as a man, I can't understand that he could have done anything like that. I know Goran very well. He was quiet and shy. He liked helping everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the fact that he's pleaded guilty to killing a number of Muslims, does that surprise you, in the light of your knowledge of this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I was completely surprised because, as I say, I knew Goran very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though he has extended the hand of friendship to him [sic], do you condemn what he has done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to say. Quite simply, I can't understand that Goran could have done anything like that. I cannot accept it, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, will you accept from me that he's pleaded guilty to those killings and has admitted them to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, I can accept it, that he has pleaded guilty. But I don't know how ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the light of the knowledge that he's accepted killing those people, do you condemn those killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I don't know how to express myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Would you wait there, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Greaves. Mr. Tochilovsky, for the Office of the Prosecutor, is going to ask you some questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Tochilovsky:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few questions about the financial assistance you received from Goran Jelisic. By the way, how much did he provide to you? How much money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: He would always give me enough to be able to survive and to have something with which to feed my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how much?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, 30 Deutschemarks, 50 Deutschemarks. It all depended. Sometimes I needed to buy medicines for my child, then he would pay for that. So I can't give you an exact figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon his return from Brcko, you met him in 1993, after that, he had enough money to open his own business in Bijeljina, a bookstore; is that correct? He had a bookstore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I know that he had a bookstore, but I don't know otherwise, and I didn't know where he got his money from. I didn't pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he had killed victims in a camp in Brcko and he had stolen money from those detainees in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: No. No, no, he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the money he gave you is the money from those dead victims in the camp. Did you realise that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judges may have some other questions. Judge Riad, who is to my right: Judge Riad? Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness DI. I can't say your name. Now, your husband is a Muslim too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: My husband is not a pure Muslim. How can I explain it to you? His father is a Muslim and his mother is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And in that case, around you, in your region, would a person like that be considered Muslim, or Serb? You know, for instance, for some people --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, more a Muslim. More a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: He is more a Muslim? What was his relationship with Jelisic? Was Jelisic your friend, or your husband's friend? I mean, usually one of the partners has a friend and the other accepts them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Goran Jelisic and I went to school together, so he was my friend. After, when he got to know my husband, we were friends and visited each other's homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And then he became a friend of your children, too? He loved your children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Is this one of his characteristics, that he used to be kind to children, or was it specific for your family? And why did he love your family so much?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way: Goran and I grew up together. We have known each other since we were ten years old. We went to school together. So we have spent a whole lifetime together, and I considered him to be a brother. He was a brother to me, almost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you tell your children -- was it some kind of general attitude, he would love children in particular, a man who has got a fatherly instinct, especially to children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes, he loved children.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you live in the same area where some of the crimes were committed, or you don't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Since you have known Jelisic all your life, did you follow up his career and what happened to him, what he was doing in life? Do you know something about it? Did he sometimes commit crimes? Did he sometimes -- apart from his love, of course, for your children, did he do something else in life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't follow it. What was important to me was that whenever I saw him, we'd always have a chat. He would come, and as I have just said, I thought of him as a brother.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So you don't know anything about his life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, I know what he did in town and the kind of person he was towards others, what he was like with his friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You don't know what he committed in life, was he once in gaol, did he do anything; you have no idea?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You have no idea. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me turn to Judge Rodrigues. Judge Rodrigues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness DI. How many children do you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time in 1993, how many children did you have at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that, in your own words, "I know Mr. Jelisic very well," but you answered Judge Riad by saying that you did not know whether Mr. Jelisic had been convicted by a court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you also said that Mr. Jelisic helped you a great deal, financially and materially. Was Mr. Jelisic a rich man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, Goran Jelisic, his family -- how can I explain this to you? They were a sort of middle-class family. They worked, his parents worked, he worked, so that they had a sort of standard -- medium standard of living; not too well but all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1993, what kind of work was Mr. Jelisic doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, he didn't tell me about it in any details, that is to say, what he was doing, because there wasn't so much work to be had where he worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you lived in the same city as Mr. Jelisic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct, but I didn't move around much. That is to say, I spent most of my time at home and Goran would come and visit me at my home, so I didn't go about town much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But was it possible to know what Mr. Jelisic did for a job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, I didn't really know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You knew Mr. Jelisic especially through the visits that he made to you, is that correct, when he came to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In May 1992, did you know what kind of job Mr. Jelisic had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: No, no. I've just told you, I was a little further off from Bijeljina during that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Several kilometres away. That is where the settlement is from Bijeljina. I don't want to give its name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few kilometres. Well, what, a thousand kilometres, two kilometres, ten kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Thirteen kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thirteen. So you said that you knew Mr. Jelisic very well, but there are all kinds of things that you don't know. I have another question. You told us that you went to school with him, that you know Jelisic very well, that you had known him for a long time, that you were friends, he was like a brother to you. Could you tell us how Mr. Jelisic was raised? What kind of relationship did he have with his parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Mr. Jelisic had quite normal relations with his parents. He was a very well-brought-up child. On the streets, at school, at home, his behaviour was always good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was raised by his parents or was it by his grandmother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Mostly by his grandmother when he was small, a little bit -- that is to say, a little by the grandmother but more with his parents, as far as I know, because we were small then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you knew Mr. Jelisic very well. Could you tell us why he was raised mostly by his grandmother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Because his parents worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question, Witness DI, is the following: I would like to go back to Mr. Greaves' question. Knowing that Mr. Jelisic admitted being guilty of various acts, including murder, of having killed at least 12 people, what is your opinion? Does that change your opinion? Is that a surprise in respect to you? Does that change your opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: My opinion of Goran -- my opinion of Goran hasn't changed, because Goran will always be what he was before for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the more specific question that Mr. Greaves asked you is: "What is your position, what is your opinion?" Do you condemn the murders that Mr. Jelisic committed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: I don't know how to express myself. Knowing Goran, I understand that he pleaded guilty, but I just can't accept it, that a person like that, with that kind of character, could have done anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this potential for committing this type of acts was something you didn't know in Mr. Jelisic's personality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DI
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you now, I just can't understand that Goran could have done anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that was the answer that you gave Mr. Greaves, but I'm not going to insist on that question and I will stop here. Thank you very much, Witness DI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness DI. I have no further questions to ask you either. Your testimony is complete. We're going to escort you out of the courtroom. Perhaps you would like to take a five or ten-minute break, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next witness should be Witness DH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is he ready? We don't need a break, just the time it takes to escort the other witness out of the courtroom. Thank you, Witness DI. We wish you a good trip back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Sir. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to take a five-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Have the accused brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We apologise for the delay, which is my own personal fault. This is Witness -- what's the pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: DH, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Witness DH. Please check to see that this is your name that's on the piece of paper. Please do not say it out loud; simply check to see that it is your name. You are going to take an oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may now be seated. Thank you for having come at the request of the Defence as a character witness for Goran Jelisic, the accused, accused by the Office of the Prosecutor of crimes against humanity and war crimes. He is sitting to your left in this courtroom. You are protected. You asked for protective measures, and this is why you are behind these screens. You have nothing to fear. Speak without fear or hatred. Answer the Defence counsel's questions first, and then you will answer the Prosecutor's questions, and lastly the Judges'. Mr. Greaves, please proceed. Examined by Mr. Greaves:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DH, would you please tell us your ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, when it was that you first met Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Towards the end of May, beginning of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't tell us anything of where you live or the area in which you live, but how was it that you came to meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: I met Goran through my brother-in-law, or son-in-law, who lived across the River of Sava and was a friend of his, and one day he brought him to my house for coffee and a drink. We sat down, had a conversation, and this is how I met Goran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, were you aware that he was living in the area in which you were living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Afterwards I found out that he had come from Bijeljina, and that at the time, he lived in that village, not far from me, across the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he begin to visit your home on more occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Yes, he would come every day with my son-in-law for coffee. He would go fishing on the Sava River, and he would bring me fish that he had caught, and this is how we became friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you now, Witness DH, about the end of August 1992. At about that time, did Goran Jelisic come to your house on a more permanent basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: We became friends. He would bring me fish every day. And he also had some stomach problems. He was quite agitated, anxious. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted) did he talk to you about what he had been doing earlier that year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: He told me first that he was taken as a prisoner on the Croatian front, that he was tortured, mistreated, and then he managed to escape. And after that, in Bijeljina -- no, in Brcko, he worked as a reserve policeman, in fact, as an ordinary policeman, and that his superiors forced him to torture, kill people, and do all that. And he couldn't take it, and then they threatened to eliminate him, and this is why he was forced to run away. He said that he could not stand it, to torture those innocent people, to kill them; that was terrible for him. So he could not find any peace. This is why he was taking medication. He was having stomach troubles, vomiting, he couldn't sleep, he had pain in his stomach, and he kept saying that those people are innocent, they had not done anything to anyone. He would call on the telephone two or three times a day some people -- I don't know who he called; probably his superiors, and he would argue with them and tell them he could not continue doing that, he would not continue doing that, that those people were innocent. This is why he did not want to go back there, and he left Brcko and Bijelina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand by what you heard from him that he had killed other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Well, I did not understand that he killed those people, because at the time, Goran was just as young as my daughter, and I saw that he was a man -- he was a man who cried, who was taking medication to calm him down, so I -- based on that, I concluded that if he had done something, he didn't do it on his own free will. And also he would not have fled if he had wanted to continue doing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to approach it slightly differently, Witness DH, he had told you that he had killed people as part of his work earlier that year; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: He didn't tell me that personally, but I heard from the conversations when he was making phone calls to Brcko or Bijelina. I don't know where he was making those phone calls to, and I don't know who he was talking to, but I heard that he was arguing with them. And based on those conversations, this is the conclusion that I made, but I didn't want to discuss it with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To you, did he ever express any remorse about what he had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: I stated that he cried a lot, and he was sorry for those people who, without any fault of theirs, were killed and tortured. And whether he was the one who killed them, or anybody else, I really cannot tell you. I could not tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he go to, without mentioning the names of the people or villages, but did he go to a place nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted) at one point he even found an apartment. He wanted to open up a shop and proceed with that, but he had not done it, although he wished -- I think he greatly desired to go back to his house. And he asked me how could I help him to cross without police, his police, arresting him, because they threatened to eliminate him. And then I already told you that I worked in the medical field, and we came up with the idea for me to go to the orthopaedics department and to take some plaster and take the nurse, bring the nurse who would put his leg into a cast and thus help him cross into his town. And that's what we did. I went to the nurse, and we took some plaster cast, and on my balcony, we put his leg into the cast. I think he didn't even wait to make sure that it was dry enough. He simply called the cab, got into the cab, and I didn't see him afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of putting a cast on his leg? What was your reasoning behind that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Well, he wanted to go back to Bijeljina or Brcko. I don't know where. Probably to Bijeljina. And the purpose of putting the cast was so that his police at the checkpoint, at the crossing, would not arrest him, because he wanted to show that he had hurt his leg. And I don't know exactly why, but he asked me to help him in this way, to do something of this kind, to help him to go back. As I said, he left, and I haven't heard anything of him afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Would you wait there, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Greaves, for being concise. Turning to the Office of the Prosecutor now, who is going to ask you the questions it deems appropriate. Mr. Nice, please proceed. Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long altogether did you know this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: From the end of May until mid-September 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first passage of time when he called at your house, he was introduced really by your son-in-law; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is your son-in-law now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: In the village across from the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he's fit and able to travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: My son-in-law or who? Can you please --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your son-in-law, he's fit and able to travel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He, of course, can give a better account than you of how it was that he met Jelisic and how Jelisic came to knock at your door; would that be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Well, he brought him. They were friends in that village. I don't know who Jelisic came to visit in that village. But this is where they met, became friends, so he would come and visit me daily. And as I said, they went fishing on the Sava, and this is how he spent his free time, relaxed. And since I loved fish, he would come every day and bring me fish, and he would stay, have coffee, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand it correctly, no explanation was given for the sudden appearance on the scene of this man at the end of May. The man, however, appeared to be perfectly normal, relaxed, and happy at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: You have Goran in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question? I didn't quite understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. I'll break it into two parts. First, no explanation was given for the sudden appearance, on your local scene, of Jelisic; he just appeared as a friend of your son-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Yes. When he came as a friend of my son-in-law, he told me that he had been taken in -- that he had been imprisoned in the Croatian front, that he was tortured there, that he managed to flee from that front. Then later on, he told me that he was in the reserve police as an ordinary policeman in Brcko, and then he told me that his superiors --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to come to all that in a minute. I want to do things in order, you see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when he first came at the end of May, he was happy and content and able to go fishing and be just an ordinary friend of your son-in-law; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: He did not look content and normal. As I've already mentioned, he was very anxious. He was taking medication. He had stomach pain. And then later on, he told me that he was in the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But to begin with, he was able to function, fishing and going out and talking to you, in an ordinary way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Yes, when -- after he had taken some medication to calm himself down. Fishing helped him relax, so that he wouldn't think about what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: (redacted) And as I said, he also wanted, in this place where I lived, to open some kind of a shop, and that would make things easier for him, since he visited the village daily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many kilometres, roughly, is your village from Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: From Brcko, approximately 90, a hundred kilometres. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the time of Jelisic's arrival in your village, had rumours, stories, news reports of the killings in Brcko reached your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did rumours, or stories, or news reports about the atrocities in Brcko first reach your village, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Well, once we learned anything, it was from television. And I don't normally read the newspapers, so I typically just followed television and radio, and they didn't really go into great detail, not enough for me to learn more about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that even at the distance of 90 or a hundred kilometres from Brcko, the killings there were something of which you remained ignorant for years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that you never heard of the photographs of the killings at Brcko and never heard that the man Jelisic, known as Adolf, was associated with those killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not even until this very moment when you're sitting here in this court, you've never heard of those things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DH
utterances.text: Well, now when I was called to come here to give testimony, then, of course, I had heard by that time, and, yes, I'm sorry. I also, at one occasion in Zvornik, I'm not quite sure where, I read in the newspapers Goran Jelisic and another man were mentioned as -- I'm not quite sure how to put this -- that they had committed killings and all that.
