utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you then feel able to go home in safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Because I believed him. I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you about what had been taking place in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: No. He just said that it was a madhouse, but that it would all pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequently, did you spend a period away from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to Bijeljina in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned, did you learn anything from your wife -- and don't tell us what her name is -- did you learn anything from your wife about Goran Jelisic and what he had done in your absence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: She told me that he came by several times and helped her by bringing her food and giving her some money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn from any other Muslims anything about Goran Jelisic visiting them? Again, don't tell us any names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of what you had found out, did you say anything to Goran about what he had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having heard that Goran Jelisic had given some assistance to your family, did you speak to him about that assistance? Did you say anything to him about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: I thanked him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you have a son, and again, don't tell us his name, but is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your son have some medical problems at around this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes, he had to have a spleen operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that, did you make efforts to leave the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to leave the former Yugoslavia, or were you prevented?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: I was prevented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to return to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the illness of your son, did you receive any assistance from Goran Jelisic in relation to that illness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: He helped me, because he took my child to the doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he pay for any of the medical treatment that your son received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Well, yes, he saw to all the costs, whatever they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard at any stage any rumours, gossip, about events that had taken place in Brcko concerning Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of what you had heard, did you ask him anything about those matters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you ask him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: I asked him whether it was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes, he acknowledged that it was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give to you any explanation as to why he had behaved in that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Well, he said he was forced to, that he had to do that, that he was threatened that he would be killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he identify anybody who had been involved in threatening him in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: He mentioned names, but I didn't remember them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything about his feelings towards what he had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Well, I noticed by his demeanour that it wasn't easy for him to say it and to talk about it. This could be felt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from yourself, were there any other people who had worked with you at the agricultural works to whom Goran Jelisic, within your knowledge, gave assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they all Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Would you wait there, please, Witness DG.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed, Mr. Nice. Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You asked him whether the rumours were true. What were the rumours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Well, about killings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are killings and there are different types of killings. What killings were the subject of rumours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Murders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the rumours specify how the murders were committed? Help us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter would like to ask the witness to speak up, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the rumours specify how the murders were committed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: No, they didn't, just that there were killings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're telling the Chamber, are you, there was no -- no rumours had escaped from Brcko about how people were being taken out and shot at random; nothing like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: No, nothing like that. At least I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so how was Jelisic's name linked with these nonspecific rumours, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard the rumours, you're telling us about the rumours. Please, what were the rumours? What did they amount to, so far as Jelisic was concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Well, they just talked about killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Try to concentrate on the question. The question was asked, and it's specific. Try to answer it. Mr. Jelisic is your friend, you knew him, you were in his house. You're under oath. Try to answer the questions specifically and precisely, please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Think back. Is there any detail of these rumours that you can now remember, please, Witness DG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything else. I just heard about the killings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, did the rumours include the fact that Jelisic was going by the name of "the Serbian Adolf"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've never heard the nickname "Adolf" used in relation to Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all he told you, unless I've misunderstood you, all he told you was that he had to do these killings because he had been threatened that he would be killed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're sure about that, that he was threatened that he would be killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Well, I believe that that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what he told you, that he was threatened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: People from SDS, leadership, police. That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was a clear and comprehensive account of his being threatened with death if he didn't murder other people; is that your account?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Jelisic has been interviewed extensively by investigators, and he's made it quite plain to those investigators that there were no threats made to him at all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: I don't know what he told them. I know what he said to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, you would accept the best person to tell us whether there were threats or not is Jelisic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: What Jelisic told me was that there were threats. Now, as to what he admitted here, I really don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we go into private session just very briefly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that Jelisic was threatened by leadership of the SDS. Are you aware that he had been a member of the SDS himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Not SDS. Police and leadership of SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife was visited by Jelisic when you were in prison. Over what period of time did he visit your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Four or five times, he came to visit her. But at what period of time exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his particular interest in your family that he wanted to help your family, please, Witness DG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Since we were good friends, that was probably the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time in '93 was this?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter didn't understand what the witness said. Could he repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time in '93 was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: When I came out of imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. When did you come out of prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: January 13, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So by that time Jelisic already knew he was a wanted man, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: I don't know if he knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in prison as part of the war or for other reasons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: Prisoner of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We've probably got your date of birth. Can you just confirm it? What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DG, are you fit and healthy today or is there anything troubling you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you yourself ever been in trouble with the police for any matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say "No" or "Yes"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DG
utterances.text: "No."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Greaves, do you wish to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I have no questions in re-examination. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me turn to my colleagues. Judge Riad. Judge Rodrigues doesn't have any questions; nor do I. Witness DG, I thank you for having come to The Hague. We have now concluded your testimony. You will be escorted out of the courtroom. The Judges will withdraw, and we will resume through videolink conference tomorrow morning at 10.00. At 10.00, I want to deal with the question that Mr. Greaves raised with Mr. Nice, but at 10.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm at the Court's disposal now or tomorrow. I know the Court was going to make an order about tomorrow's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm thinking about the interpreters. I think that the interpreters are tired. They've worked a great deal; they've worked overtime today even. I want to thank them. So I think that we will wait until tomorrow morning, until 10.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of November, 1999, at 10.00 a.m.
